hook.en: Push a magnet into a coil and a galvanometer kicks. Hold it still and nothing happens. Only a changing *magnetic flux* makes a current, and every power station runs on this idea.

title.en: Find magnetic flux through a coil.

say.en: Push a magnet into a coil and a galvanometer kicks. Hold it still and nothing happens. Only a changing magnetic flux makes a current, and every power station runs on this idea. In this lesson: Describe Faraday's and Henry's experiments.
Find magnetic flux through a coil.
Use Faraday's law epsilon equals -N dΦ/dt.

body.en: The *magnetic flux* through a plane area A in a uniform field B is $\Phi_B = BA\cos\theta$, θ being the angle between B and the normal to the area. Unit: weber (1 Wb = 1 T m²). The flux can change if B changes, if the area changes, or if the coil turns (θ changes).
body.kn: ಕಾಂತೀಯ ಅಭಿವಾಹ Φ = BA cosθ, ಏಕಮಾನ ವೆಬರ್. B, A ಅಥವಾ θ ಬದಲಾದರೆ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: Change B, A or θ to change Φ

narration.en: Magnetic flux is B times A times cos theta, measured in weber. It changes when the field, the area or the angle changes.
narration.kn: ಕಾಂತೀಯ ಅಭಿವಾಹ Φ = BA cosθ, ಏಕಮಾನ ವೆಬರ್. B, A ಅಥವಾ θ ಬದಲಾದರೆ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Magnetic flux is B times A times cos theta, measured in weber. It changes when the field, the area or the angle changes. Φ_B equals BA cos theta.

say.en: 1 Wb equals 1 T m squared.
Change B, A or theta to change Φ.

title.en: On the board: flux and Faraday's law

narration.en: Push a magnet into a coil: the galvanometer kicks while the magnet moves, and stops when it stops. The magnetic flux through a loop is Φ = BA cos θ, measured in weber. Faraday's law: the induced emf equals the rate of change of flux linkage, ε = −N dΦ/dt. If the flux rises steadily for a while and then stays constant... ...the emf is constant while the flux changes, and zero once it stops changing. Example: 50 turns of area 0.02 m², with B falling from 0.4 T to zero in 0.1 s, give ε = 50 × 0.02 × 0.4 / 0.1 = 4 V.

title.en: Move a magnet near a coil

narration.en: As the magnet moves, the flux Φ through the coil changes and an emf ε = −N dΦ/dt appears. The needle swings only while the magnet moves; it swings the other way when the magnet goes back. Faster motion or more turns give a bigger emf. The graph traces ε against time.

body.en: Faraday and Henry found that a current is induced in a coil whenever the magnetic flux through it changes: when a magnet moves relative to the coil, or when the current in a nearby coil is switched on, off or changed. *Faraday's* law: the induced emf equals the rate of change of flux. For a coil of N turns, $\varepsilon = -N\,d\Phi_B/dt$. The minus sign expresses Lenz's law.
body.kn: ಸುರುಳಿಯ ಮೂಲಕ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ಬದಲಾದಾಗಲೆಲ್ಲಾ ವಿ.ಚಾ.ಬ. ಪ್ರೇರಿತವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ: ε = −N dΦ/dt. ಋಣ ಚಿಹ್ನೆ ಲೆನ್ಜ್ ನಿಯಮ.

points.en: Moving magnet or changing current nearby → induced current

tagline.en: Magnetic flux, the induced emf and its direction, and the charge that flows through a coil.

say.en: $\Phi = BA\cos\theta$; unit weber.
$\varepsilon = -N\,d\Phi/dt$; the minus sign is Lenz's law.
Lenz's law follows from conservation of energy.
Charge through the circuit $q = N\Delta\Phi/R$, independent of time taken.

problem.en: A square loop of side 10 cm and resistance 0.5 Ω is in a uniform field of 0.10 T at 45° to its normal. The field is reduced steadily to zero in 0.70 s. Find the induced emf and current.

steps.en: Initial flux Φ = BA cos 45° = 0.1 × 0.01 × 0.707 = 7.07 × 10⁻⁴ Wb.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A square loop of side 10 cm and resistance 0.5 Ω is in a uniform field of 0.10 T at 45° to its normal. The field is reduced steadily to zero in 0.70 s. Find the induced emf and current.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A square loop of side 10 centimetres and resistance 0.5 ohms is in a uniform field of 0.10 T at 45 degrees to its normal. The field is reduced steadily to zero in 0.70 seconds. Find the induced emf and current.
Initial flux Φ equals BA cos 45 degrees equals 0.1 times 0.01 times 0.707 equals 7.07 times 10 to the power minus 4 Wb.
epsilon equals delta Φ/delta t equals 7.07 times 10 to the power minus 4 over 0.70 is approximately 1.0 times 10 to the power minus 3 volts.
I equals epsilon /R equals 1.0 times 10 to the power minus 3 over 0.5 equals 2 times 10 to the power minus 3 A.
So the answer is epsilon is approximately 1 mV; I equals 2 milliamperes.

problem.en: A coil of 100 turns and area 0.02 m² has its plane perpendicular to a field that falls from 0.5 T to 0.1 T in 0.2 s. Find the average induced emf.

steps.en: ΔΦ per turn = ΔB × A = 0.4 × 0.02 = 8 × 10⁻³ Wb.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A coil of 100 turns and area 0.02 m² has its plane perpendicular to a field that falls from 0.5 T to 0.1 T in 0.2 s. Find the average induced emf.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A coil of 100 turns and area 0.02 square metres has its plane perpendicular to a field that falls from 0.5 T to 0.1 T in 0.2 seconds. Find the average induced emf.
delta Φ per turn equals delta B times A equals 0.4 times 0.02 equals 8 times 10 to the power minus 3 Wb.
epsilon equals Ndelta Φ/delta t equals 100 times 8 times 10 to the power minus 3 over 0.2.
epsilon equals 4 volts.
So the answer is 4 volts.

heading.en: Induced charge does not depend on time

body.en: Total charge driven round a coil of resistance R is Q = NΔΦ/R. Whether you pull the magnet out fast or slowly, the same charge flows; only the current and emf change.
